name: stern_multipost_1603
title: Stern et al. multi-post and regulating-vane TM010-like cavities (COMSOL trade study)

software.boundary: impedance boundary condition (copper walls, posts, vanes)
software.mesh_notes: ~20k tetrahedra per model (text p.4); authors note convergence difficulties near field transitions may exaggerate bumps

geometry.description: Right circular cylinder R = 50 mm, d = 250 mm (aspect d/R = 5); metal posts or vanes run the full length with no end gaps. N_stat stationary + N_mov moving posts; moving posts rotate rigidly about the cavity axis on a circle of radius R_MOV, stationary posts on radius R_STAT, all posts of diameter POST_DIA (Table I). Vanes: "inner vane rounds" at R_INNER, "outer vane rounds" at R_OUTER, "vane angle" between the vane sides (teardrop/wedge shape, inset Fig. 7b).

post_and_vane_dims.value: see reference_values.tables (Table I), ratios to R

moving_post_angle_range.note: only endpoint sketches in Fig. 4/Fig. 5; see gaps

angular_phase_stationary_vs_moving.source: not given; Figs. 4-5 show equal spacing within each set

vane_round_radii.note: inferred r_round = R_x * sin(vane_angle/2) if sides are radial

walls_posts_vanes.source: Fig. 6/7 captions "temperature of 300 K"; sigma not stated; the FoM check does not constrain it (5.8e7-6.0e7 S/m depending on the Lambda0 rounding, see fom_consistency_check); use 5.8e7

conventions.form_factor_definition: C = |int B0.E dV|^2 / (B0^2 V int eps |E|^2 dV) (Eq. 3, uniform B0 || z); C0 = 0.692 for the empty TM010 reference. V convention (full cylinder vs vacuum excluding posts) NOT stated - see gaps; report C both ways
conventions.Q_definition: Q0 = omega U / P_loss (Eq. 9), impedance BC; plotted for R = 5 cm, d = 25 cm, 300 K. Scale Q as R^(1/2) (normal skin) or R^(2/3) (ASE)
conventions.notes: Lambda = f*R (GHz m), scalable; figure of merit F (Eq. 18) compares to an empty cylinder of equal TM010 frequency and equal height d = 25 cm

tables.description: Scalable geometry of the best designs (all rotate about the cavity axis)
Vane designs; vane angle in units of pi rad

fom_consistency_check.formula: F = (Lambda/Lambda0) * sqrt(C/C0) * (Q/Q_ref)^(1/4), Lambda0 = x01 c/(2 pi) = 0.11474 GHz m (printed as 0.115 on p.5), C0 = 0.692, Q_ref = (R0/delta)/(1 + R0/d) for an empty cylinder of radius R0 = x01 c/(2 pi f), height d = 0.25 m, same delta (reconstruction of Eqs. 17-26; the extracted PDF text of these equations is garbled)
fom_consistency_check.conclusion: the digitized F is reproduced from the digitized Q and C to 0.25% rms, confirming the formula reconstruction and the digitization. sigma is NOT constrained by this check: F ~ sigma^(-1/8), so the fitted sigma is degenerate with the rounding of Lambda0 - exact Lambda0 gives sigma_fit = 5.93e+07 S/m, the printed Lambda0 = 0.115 gives 5.82e+07 S/m (mean residual at 5.8e7: +0.27% vs +0.04%). Treat sigma as 5.8e7-6.0e7 S/m; recommended 5.8e7 with Lambda0 = 0.115

measured_values.note: none: the paper has no measurements

gaps.parameter: moving-post / vane rotation range (start and end angle) and the angular phase between stationary and moving sets
gaps.issue: only the end configurations are sketched (Fig. 4, Fig. 5 insets); no angles are given
gaps.proposal: parametrize by the relative rotation angle phi of the moving set; sweep phi over its full geometric range (from contact/minimum clearance to the symmetric position) at ~1 deg steps, track TM010-like by overlap, then compare along Lambda (both Q, C and F are plotted vs Lambda, so the unknown phi mapping drops out); use the digitized Lambda_min/Lambda_max of each design to locate the endpoints

gaps.parameter: vane shape (round radii, whether the sides are radial)
gaps.issue: only R_INNER, R_OUTER and the side angle are given
gaps.proposal: assume a teardrop: two circles centred at R_INNER and R_OUTER tangent to two straight sides that meet at the axis with opening angle (vane_angle*pi); check against the Fig. 5d-f / Fig. 7b inset images; vane designs are lower priority

gaps.issue: not stated; the FoM check is degenerate with the Lambda0 rounding, so it does not pin sigma
gaps.proposal: use sigma = 5.8e7 S/m (300 K); the plausible range 5.8e7-6.0e7 moves Q by <= 1.7% (Q ~ sqrt(sigma)) - carry that as a Q systematic

gaps.issue: Eq. 3 divides by "V" without saying whether V is the full cylinder (pi R^2 d) or the vacuum volume excluding the posts/vanes. The posts occupy a large area fraction: A 12.2%, B 9.0%, C 12.2%, D 9.4%, E 21.1%, F 11.3%, G 13.5%, H 7.0%, J 5.4%, K 8.0% of pi R^2, so the two conventions differ by that factor (C_vac = C_full / (1 - a))
gaps.proposal: axionFEM must report C both ways (C_full with V = pi R^2 d, C_vac with V = vacuum volume) for every Stern design; neither is preferred a priori. C0 = 0.692 (empty cylinder) does not discriminate. If one convention matches across designs with very different area fractions (D 9% vs E 21%), record it here

gaps.parameter: geometry of the "6 Post Design H" in Fig. 6b
gaps.issue: Table I has no 6-post design H (see inconsistencies)
gaps.proposal: skip this series; it has no geometry

inconsistencies.description: Design labels differ between Table I and Figs. 6-7
inconsistencies.evidence: Table I lists post designs A-H, J, K (no I): H = 4 stationary + 3 moving (7 posts). Fig. 6b plots "6 Post Design H" (5 six-post series D-H while the table has 4: D-G); Fig. 7a plots "7 Post Design I" and "7 Post Design J" and "8 Post Design K".
inconsistencies.proposal: map Table H (7-post) -> Fig. 7a "Design I"; Table J -> Fig. 7a J; Table K -> Fig. 7a K; Fig. 6b "H" has no geometry. Do not use I/H/K as a benchmark before checking this (see also the Fig. 7a inset vs Table I K item)

inconsistencies.description: Fig. 7a 8-post inset geometry vs Table I design K
inconsistencies.evidence: the Fig. 7a inset (p.8, the only 8-post design, i.e. K) shows two rings of 4 posts at ~0.31 R and ~0.65 R with post diameter ~0.2 R (re-measured on the embedded bitmap: inner posts ~26 px, outer ~55 px from the centre of an ~85 px radius disk, posts ~18 px across), but Table I gives K = R_MOV/R = R_STAT/R = 0.55, POST_DIA/R = 0.20 (one ring). The Fig. 6b 6-post inset measures 0.37/0.64/0.24 R = Table I design D (0.375/0.625/0.25), so the insets are drawn to scale and the K mismatch is real
inconsistencies.proposal: treat the design K geometry as uncertain (Table I and the inset disagree); do not use K (nor I/H) as a benchmark until the geometry is resolved; if used, run both the Table I and the inset geometry

inconsistencies.description: Some Fig. 7a design J points fall below the Q axis limit
inconsistencies.evidence: the last J point (Lambda ~0.316) is outside the Q panel (Q < 10,000) but present in the C and F panels
inconsistencies.proposal: use C/F at that point only; Q for it is not recoverable

inconsistencies.evidence: its summary (R = 5 cm, H = 25 cm, COMSOL 4.2, ~20k tets, Table I A = 2/2/0.413/0.413/0.350, ten post + three vane designs) matches the PDF

solver_class.reason: posts/vanes are off-axis, so no axisymmetry; but they run the full height with no gaps, so the TM010-like mode is z-invariant: f and C follow from a 2D scalar Helmholtz problem for Ez on the cross-section (Dirichlet on all metal), and Q adds the analytic end-cap term 1/Q = 1/Q_wall + delta/d. A 3D extruded mesh also works (the paper used 3D). axionFEM currently has no 2D planar scalar solver -> 3D unless one is added

priority_reason: tuning-angle mapping unknown, label inconsistencies (H/I, K inset vs table) and C volume convention unknown (posts 9-21% of the area); curves digitized to ~0.5% of full scale; good test of multi-rod mode tracking (A-G, J, L-N), not of absolute accuracy

readme_row.quantities: Q0, C, FoM vs Lambda=f*R: 14 digitized series (13 Table I designs + the geometry-less Fig. 6b "H"), 256 points (241 excluding "H"); Table I geometry ratios
readme_row.axisym_2d: no (2D cross-section scalar Helmholtz would suffice: z-invariant)
